text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Insurer Axa may reveal an offer for rival UAP today which could take the form of a share exchange. UAP shares have risen on rumours of a merger that would create the world's largest insurance company.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe calls for more flexibility for employers to hire or dismiss staff.
-- State expects to earn up to 25 billion francs from planned privatisation sale of 20 percent of telecoms operator France Telecom, planned for April 1997.
-- Former Economy Minister Alain Madelin, in an interview, calls for reduced taxes and administrative deregulation to boost employment.
-- French and British stock exchange watchdogs to investigate alleged insider's trading on Eurotunnel shares at the time of its 1994 recapitalisation.
-- EDF and GEC Alsthom win a three-billion-franc contract to build a coal-driven electricity plant in China.
-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis orders lease and retail store Crazy George's to provide better client information on the final cost of goods purchased after leasing.
-- SNCF state railways launches a customer loyalty programme on the Eurostar train from Paris to London.
-- Rating agency Standard and Poor's expects interest rates to rise in Europe after the shift to a single currency in 1998.
-- Germany threatens to block agreement on key preparations for monetary union unless its European partners accept tighter rules to reduce budget deficits.
